added: ===Preparing the Dough===

#Collect your ingredients.  For a basic bread, you will need 3 cups of all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon of active dry yeast, 2 teaspoons of salt and 1 2/3 cups of warm water.  These are the base ingredients, but you can add herbs to your taste.  Some suitable herbs might be rosemary or thyme.<ref>http://allrecipes.com/recipe/214751/no-knead-artisan-style-bread/</ref>[[Image:Bake Bread on the Stovetop Step 6 Version 4.jpg|center]]
#*For smaller loaf pans, you may need to cut this recipe in half.

#Combine your ingredients in a mixing bowl.  Mix the dry ingredients together before folding in the warm water.  Turn the dough until everything is fully mixed.  The dough should be slightly sticky.

{{whvid|Bake Bread on the Stovetop Step 7.360p.mp4|Bake Bread on the Stovetop Step 7-preview.jpg|Bake Bread on the Stovetop Step 7 Version 4.jpg}}

#Allow the dough to rest.  Cover bowl with plastic wrap and leave it on the countertop for 18-24 hours.  The yeast will allow the dough to rise during this time.  It may also create visible bubbles on the surface of the dough.

{{whvid|Bake Bread on the Stovetop Step 8.360p.mp4|Bake Bread on the Stovetop Step 8-preview.jpg|Bake Bread on the Stovetop Step 8 Version 2.jpg}}

#Finish the dough.  Remove it from the bowl and place it on a floured surface. Fold the ball of dough in half, then tuck the edges underneath. Pushing and folding releases the air in the dough and relaxes the gluten that is needed for the bread to keep its shape.[v162092_b01]. 11 March 2022.  Wrap this dough in a floured kitchen towel and allow it to rise for another 2 hours until you can poke your finger in about an inch and the dough bounces back.

{{whvid|Bake Bread on the Stovetop Step 9.360p.mp4|Bake Bread on the Stovetop Step 9-preview.jpg|Bake Bread on the Stovetop Step 9 Version 2.jpg}}
===Baking the Bread on the Stovetop===

#Preheat the dutch oven.  Place the dutch oven on your largest burner.  Put the thermal ballast in the bottom of the pot and cover it with both lids.  Turn the burner on high heat.  Allow the heat to rise within the oven for 5 minutes.  After five minutes, reduce the heat to just above medium.[[Image:Bake Bread on the Stovetop Step 10 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Place the dough in your floured baking pan.  You want to flour all parts of the inside of the pan.  It is helpful to rub oil or lard on the inside for the flour to stick to, then pour the flour in, turn and shake the pan until it is completely covered on the inside.  The dough should fit well in the pan.  The dough will rise more during baking, so it should not exceed the top of the pan.[[Image:Bake Bread on the Stovetop Step 11 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#*Another option to covering the pan with flour is using oatmeal.  Pour oil in the pan covering the bottom and sides, then pour finely ground oatmeal in the pan.  Twisting your wrist, be sure to turn and shake the pan until all the sides are also covered in oatmeal.

#Place the pan inside your dutch oven.  Using an oven mitt, remove the lids of the dutch oven and set them aside on a heat-proof surface.  Carefully place your loaf pan in the center of the dutch oven, avoiding the hot sides.  Make sure there is enough room on all sides of the pan for heat to surround it.

{{whvid|Bake Bread on the Stovetop Step 12.360p.mp4|Bake Bread on the Stovetop Step 12-preview.jpg|Bake Bread on the Stovetop Step 12 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bake the bread.  Using oven mitts, place both of the lids back on top of the dutch oven.  Bake the bread for about 30 minutes.  Check it after 20 minutes to see if it seems to be gaining a crust.  The top of the bread will not brown, but it should no longer be soft and doughy once it is cooked.[[Image:Bake Bread on the Stovetop Step 13 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Place the bread on a cooling rack.  Remove the lids and the pan from the dutch oven using oven mitts.  Carefully shake the bread out of the pan.  It should fall out easily because you floured your pan.  The bottom of the bread will be significantly more cooked than the top.[[Image:Bake Bread on the Stovetop Step 14 Version 2.jpg|center]]
#*If you don’t have a cooling rack, you can cool the bread on another heat-proof surface like a plate.

==Steps==
===Creating a Dutch Oven===

#*Try using some broken pieces of thick tile.  Flat, or smallish round stones would work as well.
#*Another option is re-purposing an empty tuna can.  Make sure that the paper is removed and place it in the bottom of the pot.

#Find a bread pan to fit inside your pot.  You may use a Pyrex or equivalent (not ordinary glass) bowl which can withstand the heat, or a metal or ceramic bread pan.  Place the pan in the pot, on top of the ballast.  If you are using a rectangular loaf pan.  Make sure that the long sides fit within your pot and the height of the pan should not exceed the rim of the pot.<ref>http://www.goodhousekeeping.com/cooking-tools/bakeware-reviews/a18954/best-loaf-pans/</ref>[[Image:Almost_ready.jpg|center]]

#*If you are having a difficult time finding a lid which fits, try using another pan large enough to cover the top of the pot.

#Place the dough in your floured baking pan.  You want to flour all parts of the inside of the pan.  It is helpful to rub oil or lard on the inside for the flour to stick to, then pour the flour in, turn and shake the pan until it is completely covered on the inside.  The dough should fit well within the pan.  The dough will rise more during baking, so it should not exceed the top of the pan.

removed: {{fa}}Baking bread on the stovetop is a great alternative to using the oven.  Baking on the stovetop can be an energy saver,<ref>http://www.sustainweb.org/realbread/homebake/</ref> as well as a useful alternative when an oven is not available. This process can be used at home, over a camping stove, or in a boat galley to deliver a fresh loaf right to your table.
==steps==
===Creating a Dutch Oven===

#Start with a large pot.  The heavier the material, the better.  You will be cooking dry, so cast iron is preferable.  If you choose to use something lighter, like aluminum, consider using this pot only for baking on the stovetop, since the bottom will likely become slightly burnt.<ref>http://www.thekitchn.com/dutch-ovens-how-to-choose-and-134398</ref>

#Place an old tuna can in the bottom and center of the pot.  This will become the base where your bread pan will rest, and allow for air to move around the pan.  It also keeps the pan from sitting directly on the heat to reduce the amount of burn on the bottom of the loaf.

#Find a bread pan to fit inside your pot.  Typically you will want a rectangular loaf pan.  Make sure that the long sides fit within your pot and the height of the pan should not exceed the rim of the pot.<ref>http://www.goodhousekeeping.com/cooking-tools/bakeware-reviews/a18954/best-loaf-pans/</ref>
#*It should not fit too snug.  You need space for air to flow all the way around the loaf pan.

#*If your loaf pan is small enough, you may be able to fit two of them inside the dutch oven.  Add another tuna can and bake two loaves at the same time.  Slightly increase the cook time by 5-10 minutes to accommodate the extra loaf.
#Fit a lid to your pot.  This lid should have enough clearance to allow the bread pan to fit, while leaving room for the bread to rise over the top of the pan.  Test it with a bread pan in place.
#*If you are having a difficult time finding a lid which fits, try using another pan large enough to cover the top of the pot.
#*Don’t worry about having a tight fit.  If there is a little space, this will allow for some of the steam to be released and assist in hardening your crust.

#Cover the lid with another lid.  It is important to do all you can to keep as much heat as possible inside the dutch oven.  Since heat rises, it is helpful to cover the the lid or pan with a second lid to force the heat back down toward the oven.<ref>http://scienceline.ucsb.edu/getkey.php?key=3901</ref>

#*Rather than creating your own dutch oven, another option is purchasing an Omnia Stovetop Oven, which is created for this purpose.<ref>http://www.amazon.com/Omnia-Oven-stove-solution-wonder/product-reviews/B000YLJQ5U</ref>
===Preparing the Dough===

#Collect your ingredients.  For a basic bread, you will need 3 cups of all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon of active dry yeast, 2 teaspoons of salt and 1 2/3 cups of warm water.  These are the base ingredients, but you can add herbs to your taste.  Some herbs might be rosemary or thyme.<ref>http://allrecipes.com/recipe/214751/no-knead-artisan-style-bread/</ref>
#*For smaller loaf pans, you may need to cut this recipe in half.
#Combine your ingredients in a mixing bowl.   Mix the dry ingredients together before folding in the warm water.  Turn the dough until everything is fully mixed.  The dough should be slightly sticky.

#Allow the dough to rest.  Cover bowl with plastic wrap and leave it on the counter top for 18-24 hours.  The yeast will allow the dough to rise during this time.  It may also create visible bubbles on the surface of the dough.[[Image:Loaves_ready_to_bake.jpg|center|550px|thumb|Whole wheat bread, ready to bake.]]

#Finish the dough.  Remove it from the bowl and place it on a floured surface.  Fold the ball of dough in half, then tuck the edges underneath.  Wrap this dough in a floured kitchen towel and allow it to rise for another 2 hours until you can poke your finger in about an inch and the dough bounces back.
===Baking the Bread===

#Preheat the dutch oven.  Place the dutch oven your largest burner.  Put the tuna can in the bottom of the oven and cover it with both lids.  Turn the burner on high heat.  Allow the heat to rise within the oven for 5 minutes.  After five minutes, reduce the heat to just above medium.<ref>http://theboatgalley.com/baking-bread-stove-top-yeast-breads/</ref>

#Place the dough in your floured baking pan.  You want to flour all parts of the inside of the pan.  It is helpful to rub oil or lard on the inside for the flour to stick to, then pour the flour in, turn and shake the pan until it is completely covered on the inside.  The dough should fit well within the pan.  The dough will rise more during baking, so it should not exceed the top of the pan.

#*Another option to covering the pan with flour is using oatmeal.  Pour oil in the pan covering the bottom and sides, then pour finely ground oatmeal in the pan.  Twisting your wrist, be sure to turn and shake the pan until all the sides are also covered in oatmeal.

#Place the pan inside your dutch oven.  Using an oven mitt, remove the lids of the dutch oven and set them aside on a heat-proof surface.  Carefully place your loaf pan in the center of the dutch oven, avoiding the hot sides.  Make sure there is enough room on all sides of the pan for heat to surround it.[[Image:Almost_ready.jpg|center]]

#Bake the bread.  Using oven mitts, place both of the lids back on top of the dutch oven.  Bake the bread for about 30 minutes.  Check it after 20 minutes to see if it seems to be gaining a crust.  The top of the bread will not brown, but it should no longer be soft and doughy once it is cooked.[[Image:Baking_on_stove.jpg|center|550px|thumb|Baking in progress.]]

#Place the bread on a cooling rack.  Remove the lids and the pan from the dutch oven using oven mitts.  Carefully shake the bread out of the pan.  It should fall out easily because you floured your pan.  The bottom of the bread will be significantly more cooked than the top.
#*If you don’t have a cooling rack, you can cool the bread on another heat-proof surface like a plate.
== Tips ==
*This could work on any heat source including a campfire or a galley kitchen on a boat.
*If using a glass loaf pan, make absolutely sure it's Pyrex or a similar heat-tolerant glass, and be aware that even Pyrex can violently explode if used directly on the stovetop.
*Enameled steel pot or something with similar thermal properties (insulating, traps heat).
*An empty tuna can.
*A bread pan that will fit inside the pot without touching the sides.
*Your favorite bread recipe ingredients.
{{reflist}}

added: {{fa}}Cooking leavened bread on top of a stove seems like it should be possible, but after dozens of failed experiments one might be tempted to give up. Here is a tried-and-true method that can serve as a starting point for your own stovetop breads.
[[Category:Basic Cooking Skills]]
[[Category:Breads]]
== Steps ==

#  Mix, knead, rise, punch down, and shape your loaves as usual. Here you see an experimental method where all the steps were done in the same bowl, which will now be used for cooking as well. added: Cooking leavened [[Make Bread|bread]] on top of a stove seems like it should be possible, but after dozens of failed experiments, one might be tempted to give up. Here is a tried-and-true method that can serve as a starting point for your own stovetop breads.

#  Mix, knead, rise, punch down, and shape your loaves as usual. Here, you see an experimental method where all the steps were done in the same bowl, which will now be used for cooking as well. Form the loaves with butter on the outside to keep them from sticking to each other and the pan, and the dough will rise a second time.

[[Image:Loaves_ready_to_bake.jpg|center|550px|thumb|Whole wheat bread, ready to bake.]]

#  Line the base of a porcelain pot with thermal ballast, preferably flat, but smallish round stones would probably work as well. Here, you see some broken pieces of thick tile from a demolition site.

[[Image:Thermal_ballast.jpg|center|550px|thumb|Broken tile pieces for ballast.]]

#  Place the Pyrex or equivalent (not ordinary glass) bowl into the pot, on top of the ballast.

[[Image:Almost_ready.jpg|center|550px]]

#  If the pot lid has a steam hole in it, find a stainless steel bolt, washer, and nut to fit it. Try to keep as much heat inside the pot as possible, but remember it's not necessary.

[[Image:Closing_steam_vent.jpg|center|550px|thumb|Cost less than a dollar at the local Ace hardware in La Paz, BCS, MX in 2014.]]

# Cover and heat on high for 15 minutes or so. Expect to have a few failed loaves, uncooked in the middle, or overcooked, if your equipment is different from that shown. Your stove provides more or less heat, or if you attempt much larger or much smaller loaves. Make sure you have time, but it may need to be varied accordingly.

[[Image:Baking_on_stove.jpg|center|550px|thumb|Baking in progress.]]

#  Carefully (it's hot!) place the pot in the sun if that's an option, and cover as much of it as possible with insulating materials as for a [[Use a Suitcase as a Haybox|haybox]]. Use a durable natural fabric like cotton underneath the hot pan.

[[Image:Hayboxed.jpg|center|550px|thumb|Covered with wool coat and padded laptop case.]]

# Leave for an hour or more. Consider several hours, as it gives a better chance of success and cannot hurt it. When time is up, or you just get too hungry to wait, uncover the pot carefully.

[[Image:Removed_heatbox.jpg|center|550px]]

# [[Slice Bread|Cut open]] a [[Make a Loaf of White Bread|loaf]] and check for doneness. If overdone or underdone, make a note of it and adjust stovetop time accordingly in the next try. If it's perfect, as shown here, enjoy the rewards. You have saved up to 80% of the fuel necessary to bake the same loaf in the oven.

[[Image:Perfectly_baked_bread.jpg|center|550px|thumb|Mmmmm, perfect.]]

*When moving the pot from the stovetop after the cooking time is up, remember that it could be 300° F or more, which is very hot! Use leather gloves, potholders, or the equivalent, and test first by gripping without lifting.

*Pot

*Natural fabric

== Tips ==
*This could work on any heat source including a campfire, and this setup is much lighter to carry than a dutch oven. Find the ballast stones at the campsite.
== Warnings ==
*If using glass, make absolutely sure it's Pyrex or a similar heat-tolerant glass, and be aware that even Pyrex can violently explode if used directly on the stovetop.

*When moving the pot from the stovetop after the cooking time is up, remember that it could be 300 degrees Fahrenheit or more: very hot! Use leather gloves, potholders, or the equivalent, and test first by gripping without lifting.
